Same-card PRIME export/import shares the existing object and deduplicates
reimports on an open. Globally unique stable fake mmap offsets avoid collisions
with the importer's existing objects. Exported fd mappings retain the same
pages after all GEM handles and fds close. Each object also owns one shared
`DmaBufObject` reservation/name across handles and exports. DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC
START waits for conflicting native GPU accesses (a CPU reader waits for writers;
a CPU writer waits for readers and writers); END orders coherent RAM access.
DMA_BUF_SET_NAME and EXPORT_SYNC_FILE use that shared state and the common
fd reservation/copyout/install protocol. IMPORT_SYNC_FILE resolves the actual
sync-file descriptor and atomically publishes its READ/WRITE leaf batch through
the same reservation admission gate as kernel CPU copies and native jobs.
Invalid flags precede fd lookup; bad/non-sync descriptors and copy faults
publish nothing, and an empty signalled-stub batch changes no reservation.
Foreign attachments remain unavailable.

Compatibility-profile GuC and legacy Gen12 resident submissions check every
synchronous leaf's reservation, rejecting conflicting work without partial
reservation publication. The bounded BMG EXEC_OBJECT_ASYNC contract below
selectively skips prior implicit GPU waits for flagged entries. All entries
still attach their terminal CompletionFence as READ or WRITE before cache
publication. Read-only jobs may overlap. Independent LRCs have no shared ordered
dma-fence context: completing one cannot elide another's live dependency.
Resources release before terminal signalling, including failures after
reservation and verified reset. Unproven stop, timeout and cancelled waiters
retain reservations. Scheduling acknowledgments are not terminal events.
Fence status and immutable context/sequence callbacks run before the admission
gate; removed foreign references are dropped after it. Kernel CPU copies and
the synchronous subset of implicit GPU accesses require an unchanged
reservation addition generation under that gate after their outside-lock
conflict observation. ASYNC entries retain terminal fences without importing
prior GPU waits; a stale snapshot cannot remove a later live fence. A racing import therefore
refuses access without copying bytes or publishing a partial multi-object job.
Async PREAD/PWRITE wait and retry individual chunks without replaying a copied
prefix. Xe GPU execution retains its explicit-sync contract: imported ordinary
READ/WRITE fences do not create hidden GPU waits, while CPU access and sync-file
exports still observe them and every native terminal fence.
Existing raw CPU/user mappings still require the trusted submitter's exclusion
contract; a reservation cannot revoke an already installed mapping.

#### Per-object i915 implicit synchronization

`EXEC_OBJECT_ASYNC` (object bit6) is accepted on the existing live Battlemage GuC profile for ordinary system WB softpin objects. The request copies each object's flag before awaiting. All listed storage in an ASYNC request must remain ordinary WB: actual local/WC, VM-owned and pinned-user objects return EINVAL, including imported handles, before context finalization or private residency/reservation effects. Other platforms return EINVAL for ASYNC. A qualified platform without a current matching nonzero user epoch and nonempty published engines returns ENODEV. Same-card WB PRIME imports retain the same BO/reservation identity. No relocation support is added.

For an unflagged object, a read waits for previous writers and a write waits for previous readers/writers. A flagged object skips those prior implicit GPU waits in both pre-wait and final GT admission. Every object still receives the accepted job's READ/WRITE terminal fence. Mixed lists do not relax unflagged entries. Repeated internal aliases fold WRITE and required implicit synchronization with OR, then publish at most one strongest fence per BO identity. The whole mixed transaction checks all synchronous conflict decisions and their addition generations before adding any fence, under the existing common reservation gate. Concurrent PRIME imports participate in that gate; callbacks and retired-reference drops occur outside it. A stale ASYNC snapshot cannot remove a later live fence.

Explicit sync-file, binary/timeline syncobj input and previous-job same-context order remain mandatory. Mandatory page-table, leaf, LRC and ring publication is unchanged. BMG's source-qualified uncompressed two-way coherent PAT2=0xf is the initial ASYNC profile; unsupported storage/profile is refused rather than silently reverting to implicit waits. Cache/output failure signals only unpublished error fences. After acceptance, cancellation and context/BO/fd close retain native GPU state and all terminal reservations through normal retirement or proven reset, including missing acknowledgements or access/cache uncertainty. Completing a newer ASYNC job does not remove an older live fence.

Synchronized GEM PREAD/PWRITE/GEM_WAIT and PRIME CPU-sync access continue to observe all conflicting terminal reservations. Existing mmap alias lifetime is unchanged; ASYNC does not freeze or revoke arbitrary CPU stores. The client remains responsible for explicit ordering of potentially overlapping work. This contract does not add migration, MMU invalidation or USERPTR revalidation.

GEM_BUSY reports render-class readers as 0x10000 and a writer as 0x10001.
GEM_WAIT waits for readers and writers: zero polls with ETIME if busy, negative
waits indefinitely, and positive nanoseconds use one monotonic deadline retained
across async parking. Positive waits write back remaining time; timeout writes
zero. A terminal reset counts as completion for busy/wait. CPU SET_DOMAIN and
SW_FINISH also wait for conflicting reservations. Synchronous kernel dispatch
returns WouldBlock for a pending nonzero wait; primary/render `ioctl_user`
awaits without retaining IRQ-safe locks. Indefinite side-effect-free user waits
use `restart_after` when available; finite waits retain their copied deadline.
Broader accelerated presentation profiles remain separate work.

Context/VM create, destroy and scalar GET/SETPARAM have per-open namespaces,
bounded extension chains and retained VM identity after VM-handle destruction.
Every i915 extension chain (context create, ENGINES, GEM_CREATE_EXT and
execbuffer timeline fences) is walked by `intel_gpu_uapi::user_extensions`,
i915_user_extensions in its order: 512 links, the 513th E2BIG; flags then each
rsvd word copied and checked singly (EFAULT, then EINVAL); the name copied and
dispatched (EINVAL outside the caller's table); next_extension copied only
after the handler ran. There is no visited set: a cycle is applied again until
E2BIG or until its handler refuses (a LOAD_BALANCE that revisits its slot is
EEXIST).
CONTEXT_CREATE_EXT follows i915_gem_context_create_ioctl/create_setparam: each
SETPARAM link (ctx_id nonzero is EINVAL) is applied through set_proto_ctx_param
to a private proto-context when the walk reaches it, so a link's errno ends the
walk before any later link is copied. VM is looked up at its link (later handle
destruction does not unbind it); SSEU is EINVAL below 32 bytes, otherwise
ENODEV (GRAPHICS_VER != 11). The context ID is reserved only after the whole
chain applied, and any error discards the proto with no name consumed.
Context zero is implicit and, like i915 GRAPHICS_VER 12, finalized at open;
created contexts stay proto-contexts until execbuffer, GETPARAM or reset-stats
lookup. Each context owns legacy RCS0 and BCS0 states; an explicit engine map
can additionally select advertised COPY1/BCS8 and dense COMPUTE instances. CONTEXT_PARAM_ENGINES
(0xa) follows set_proto_ctx_engines: once per proto-context (EINVAL twice or
after finalization), 8-byte header plus 4-byte class/instance entries (at most
64), INVALID/INVALID_NONE holes, per-entry copy with ENOENT for absent engines
before later faults, then a bounded extension chain. LOAD_BALANCE fills an
INVALID hole with copied same-class, published dense logical siblings;
duplicate siblings, mixed/unpublished engines and malformed reserved fields
(flags, then mbz64, each copied singly) refuse before proto-map publication. An existing/out-of-range destination is
checked before sibling-body copies. Zero siblings leave a hole. Each virtual
slot uses the existing persistent GuC placement context, private physical-engine
receipt and migration-aware retirement/watchdog ownership. Bonding/parallel
remain NotImplemented; unknown extensions return EINVAL.
Duplicate ENGINES create extensions are EINVAL
before their copy; GETPARAM ENGINES is EINVAL. Each map slot is its own
`UserContext`. Execbuffer's ring field indexes the map, or selects legacy
DEFAULT/RENDER→RCS0 and BLT→BCS0. Source-qualified Gen12 main-GuC BSD/VEBOX
use the published dense media selectors described below; absent/unowned engines,
holes and out-of-range slots return EINVAL. GEM_CONTEXT_GETPARAM/SETPARAM
look the context up first (ENOENT, before any capable() question); SET
follows set_proto_ctx_param on a proto-context and ctx_setparam on a finalized
one. BANNABLE: size EINVAL, then
value 0 without CAP_SYS_ADMIN EPERM; any nonzero value sets it. RECOVERABLE:
size EINVAL, then 0 clears and any other value sets it. PRIORITY
(validate_priority): size EINVAL, ENODEV without I915_SCHEDULER_CAP_PRIORITY
(advertised while submission is live), EINVAL outside -1023..=1023 as an s64,
EPERM above 0 without CAP_SYS_NICE; capable() is asked only for an in-range
positive value. A set stores the priority and sends GuC nothing (Linux
set_priority). Every hardware member of the context, including engine-map
slots and Gen12 media members created later, registers its next job at
map_i915_prio_to_guc_prio of it: 0 is GUC_CLIENT_PRIORITY_KMD_NORMAL (2),
below 0 NORMAL (3), above 0 HIGH (1); KMD_HIGH (0) needs
I915_PRIORITY_DISPLAY and is unreachable from userspace. Each execbuffer is
queued at the context's priority at its ioctl (rq->sched.attr) and raises,
never lowers, the jobs ahead of it on the same hardware context
(__i915_schedule, guc_bump_inflight_request_prio): a raised job whose GuC
registration is enabled gets one priority-only UPDATE_CONTEXT_POLICIES
(guc_context_set_prio); a job not yet registered registers with the raise;
a job being disabled gets none. A queued request registers at its own
priority raised by the requests queued behind it. LINUX-GAP: dependencies on
other contexts' jobs (objects, fences) do not raise them.
PERSISTENCE: size EINVAL; a finalized context already in the requested state
succeeds; setting succeeds (the job watchdog is hangcheck); clearing is ENODEV
(no I915_SCHEDULER_CAP_PREEMPTION). PROTECTED_CONTENT on a proto has no size
check: 0 succeeds, nonzero is ENODEV (no PXP); finalized, it is EINVAL, as are
LOW_LATENCY, GTT_SIZE and unknown parameters. capable() is asked only where
Linux asks it, outside the namespace lock. GETPARAM never reads the input
size, reports size 0, and returns PROTECTED_CONTENT 0 and the stored,
sign-extended PRIORITY. LINUX-GAP: BANNABLE and RECOVERABLE are stored and
reported only; a reset bans every context it finds and none is recovered.
VM is settable
only on a proto-context (set_proto_ctx_vm: size EINVAL, then upper_32_bits and
the lookup ENOENT), whose engine states are never claimed; a finalized
context's VM is immutable (ctx_setparam EINVAL). QUERY has Linux's
two-pass/per-item signed-length protocol: system memory reports actual RAM;
engine info reports the live engine set with HAS_LOGICAL_INSTANCE, including
physical COPY8 mapped to logical COPY1 on BMG, otherwise zero engines; a nonzero input
num_engines/rsvd header is per-item -EINVAL. HWCONFIG returns the exact
firmware KLV bytes only after this card's GT publishes a validated snapshot;
absence returns per-item -ENODEV. Size-only queries never access the data pointer;
short capacity returns -EINVAL, failed data copies return -EFAULT and later
items still run. Only the item length is written back. Topology and geometry-DSS
queries return per-card observed fuse snapshots using the i915 topology layout;
absence returns -ENODEV. GuC submission-version returns -ENODEV until the userspace scheduling
interface is admitted; live replies contain branch=0 and the loaded CSS's
submission major/minor/patch, independently of its firmware release.
HAS_BLT, HAS_EXECBUF2/NO_RELOC/HANDLE_LUT/SOFTPIN/BATCH_FIRST/CONTEXT_ISOLATION and
HAS_ALIASING_PPGTT=3 follow live admission. HAS_EXEC_FENCE,
HAS_EXEC_FENCE_ARRAY, HAS_EXEC_SUBMIT_FENCE and HAS_EXEC_TIMELINE_FENCES,
plus DRM_CAP_SYNCOBJ and DRM_CAP_SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE, also follow live admission.
HAS_EXEC_ASYNC (43) returns 1 only for a cached current matching nonzero
Battlemage user epoch with nonempty published engines, and 0 for unavailable
state or every other profile. It performs no GT wake or MMIO. The ordinary
WB/import restrictions in the per-object contract remain mandatory; other
GETPARAM output bytes and ioctl encodings are unchanged.
Unsupported engines and their capabilities are never advertised.

The i915 compatibility GETPARAM discovery path reports observed PCI revision
(32), union DSS count (33), actual fused EU count (34), timestamp frequency
(51) and OA timestamp frequency (57: `DeviceFacts::oa_timestamp_frequency`,
the clock with Wa_18013179988's CTC shift on 12.55 and 12.70–12.74, sampled
with the clock and independent of the OA opt-in). PERF_REVISION (54) reports 1
when the OA unit is published, and 0 otherwise. Missing or mismatched topology/facts return ENODEV, never zero; immutable
facts survive a stopped GT without MMIO or wake. HAS_SCHEDULER (41) reports
ENABLED | PRIORITY (3) while live and 0 otherwise, leaving the
preemption/semaphore/busy-stat/static-priority-map capability bits clear;
context PRIORITY and PERSISTENCE checks read the same value. Obsolete UMS parameters 1/2/3/14 return ENODEV. Legacy
slice/subslice masks 46/47 return EINVAL on Xe_HP-and-later profiles, as in
Linux; callers use full topology queries.

#### i915 perf UAPI compatibility and dynamic metrics

The legacy i915 perf UAPI provides backwards compatibility for tools (such as
Intel GPA, gputop, and Mesa metrics) on render nodes:
- `DRM_IOCTL_I915_PERF_OPEN` (0x76): accepts a 16-byte `drm_i915_perf_open_param`
  structure (`flags`, `num_properties`, `properties_ptr`). Decodes property array
  entries (SAMPLE_OA, OA_METRICS_SET, OA_FORMAT, OA_EXPONENT, etc.) and allocates
  a dedicated i915-formatted stream file descriptor.
- `DRM_IOCTL_I915_PERF_ADD_CONFIG` (0x77): accepts a 72-byte `drm_i915_perf_oa_config`
  structure (`uuid`, `n_mux_regs`, `n_boolean_regs`, `n_flex_regs`, pointers to register pairs).
  Validates whitelist register addresses, requires unique UUIDs per card, allocates
  a dynamic positive config ID, and stages register sets for ring reconfiguration.
- `DRM_IOCTL_I915_PERF_REMOVE_CONFIG` (0x78): takes an 8-byte u64 config ID and
  removes an unreferenced dynamic configuration.
- Stream ioctls on the stream file descriptor:
  - `I915_PERF_IOCTL_ENABLE` (0x6900): activates OA report generation.
  - `I915_PERF_IOCTL_DISABLE` (0x6901): halts OA sampling.
  - `I915_PERF_IOCTL_CONFIG` (0x6902): accepts `arg` directly as a u64 metric set ID,
    reconfigures the OA unit, and returns the previous config ID.
- Stream reading: reports delivered through the i915 stream fd prepend an 8-byte
  `drm_i915_perf_record_header` (`type = 1` for `DRM_I915_PERF_RECORD_SAMPLE`,
  `pad = 0`, `size = 8 + report_size`).
- Query item 3 (`DRM_I915_QUERY_PERF_CONFIG`):
  - `DRM_I915_QUERY_PERF_CONFIG_LIST` (1): reports registered config count and IDs
    (`48 + 8 * n_configs` bytes).
  - `DRM_I915_QUERY_PERF_CONFIG_DATA_FOR_UUID` (2): retrieves config metadata and
    registers for a given 36-byte UUID (`48 + 72` bytes header + registers).
  - `DRM_I915_QUERY_PERF_CONFIG_DATA_FOR_ID` (3): retrieves config metadata and
    registers for a given 64-bit config ID.
  - Unknown configurations return `-ENOENT` (-2) in `item.length`. Probing with
    capacity 0 returns required buffer length without reading register pointers.

#### i915 selected capture and live diagnostic protection

`EXEC_OBJECT_CAPTURE` (object bit7) snapshots selection during raw execbuffer
admission and retains the actual selected BO mappings with the job's private
VM. Selected currently admitted WB system/same-card PRIME ranges contribute
real safe payload prefixes to the existing native-v3 `NARFVMEM` section.
Unselected objects do not disclose payload. VRAM, WC, VM-private softpin and
i915 USERPTR remain outside this profile. WRITE/ASYNC, explicit fences,
coherence, output rollback and terminal/cancel/full-reset ownership are unchanged;
existing native Xe DUMPABLE and owned pin-backed diagnostics keep their bounds.

GETPARAM HAS_EXEC_CAPTURE45 passively copies1 only for matching nonzero cached
live GuC admission, submission ABI major1 and nonempty published engines;
otherwise it succeeds with0. This bounded NARF availability policy differs from
Linux's unconditional1. It performs no wake or MMIO. Independent default-off
raw-coredump boot admission and current reader/clear capabilities still apply.

NO_ERROR_CAPTURE (context parameter4) defaults0. CREATE_EXT and SET accept size0,
including already-finalized/busy contexts; any nonzero value enables it and0
clears it. GET performs ordinary context lookup/finalization, ignores input size
and returns size0/value0or1. One live policy Arc spans every legacy RCS/BCS,
indexed physical/virtual and lazy Gen12 media member and each retained job after
namespace/fd destruction. Error capture samples each retained policy once.
If any retained i915 context is protected, NARF skips the entire NEW raw bundle
before reading log/CT, parent/child LRC/ring/group scratch, VM tables or BO bytes.
This conservative whole-bundle rule is a NARF choice because the bundle shares
global and other-job sources. Existing immutable reports/readers remain unchanged.
Normal `UserJob::capture_lanes` state saves, generic redacted fault/telemetry
paths and all terminal/recovery proofs remain active.

The existing two-permit/card, eight execution, four VM, sixteen owned-table,
eight selected-range and 16KiB/range-prefix limits remain, with explicit omitted,
truncated, refused and authority-loss data. Selection adds no capture-time flush,
reservation wait, allocation, CPU alias or storage right. This is a bounded
payload subset, not Linux full coredump/error-sysfs or implicit all-batch capture.

#### i915 automatic global-reset availability

GETPARAM HAS_GPU_RESET35 passively writes signed32 level1 only when a distinct
`UserBackend::reset_availability_epoch()` snapshot matches current nonzero GuC
user admission, platform, ABI major1 and nonempty engines. The callback refuses
by default. Its sealed one-use qualification binds the live recovery worker,
hardware incarnation, profile, exact engines and firmware-upload identity;
a boolean or a stale receipt cannot confer readiness. The actual private PPGTT
store and successful terminal retirement must be verified on every published
engine before each incarnation becomes available. Other states succeed with0;
per-engine level2, value3 and manual reset are not exposed. Querying performs
no PCI/MMIO/wake, PM resume or asynchronous action.

Observed faults withdraw readiness before owner cleanup. Existing IRQ shutdown,
bounded diagnostics, admission closure and display quarantine precede actual
hardware stop. Only verified full GuC/GT reset, firmware-DMA idle and retained
cache/media/wake handoff permit terminal retirement; only previously live,
proved-clean recovery may restart Cold. Initial qualification and failed cleanup
stay closed. There is no job replay or new reset authority. Accepted park/S3/CCS
transitions withdraw readiness; refusal which preserves Running retains it.
Clean park keeps its user epoch but reports0 until fresh qualification and
compatible epoch adoption. Worker cancellation closes user admission/readiness
while retaining uncertain DMA. This cache describes last observed software
state; actual register actions still require current authority. Native shared
coordinator/GT models do not establish full physical Owner/PCI/firmware-registry
or S3 execution.

#### i915 context frequency hints and creation publication

The i915 compatibility HAS_CONTEXT_FREQ_HINT(59) writes signed1 only for the same
cached qualified GuC profile, matching nonzero current epoch/platform, nonempty
published engine set and submission ABI major1 used by native low-latency queues.
Unsupported states return ioctl success with signed-22 as pinned i915 does; output
faults return EFAULT. This passive query performs no GT wake or MMIO and does not
promise that a later submission will still be admitted.

CONTEXT_PARAM_LOW_LATENCY0xe enables immutable per-context intent through
CREATE_EXT SETPARAM on every admitted current profile. A standalone SETPARAM can
enable only an unfinalized graphics-major12 proto-context: qualified TGL/ADL/RPL,
DG2 and MTL/ARL. BMG/LNL/PTL require the create extension. GET, default/finalized
context mutation and unsupported submission return EINVAL; a missing context
returns ENOENT. The pinned enable operation ignores size/value (even value0
turns it on), reads no value payload, and offers no disable or live toggle.
Repeated enabled proto SET is idempotent. Existing later-generation engine-map
compatibility behavior is unchanged; it does not grant late frequency mutation.

Intent is retained by every legacy RCS/BCS, indexed physical/virtual and lazily
selected admitted Gen12 media context. Engine-map creation and enabling preflight
are namespace serialized before claim, and invalid creation/copyout discards the
unpublished context. CREATE reserves a private nonce-bound name charged against the
context limit, configures its copied proto state and retained selected VM references
privately, and calls faultable copyout without the namespace IRQ lock. Only successful
copyout permits an identity-checked publication. Pending names return ENOENT to
lookup/mutation/destroy/EXEC; they cannot be claimed. Failure rolls back only that
reservation and destroys private graphs outside the lock. Serial failed-tail IDs
remain reusable; concurrent successful creators can leave opaque ID gaps.
Each actual registration/re-registration retains the existing
GuC policy request: action0x100b, SLPM_GT_FREQUENCY key0x2005/length1, bit28 for the
hint and zero ordinarily. The fast request is ordered before normal ENABLE/ACK;
there is no policy-specific ACK. Existing acknowledged global frequency/power
limits and mandatory CPU/table/leaf/LRC/ring publication are unchanged.

The hint can request more aggressive firmware frequency strategy and may affect
power use. It grants no new engines, storage/VM/CPU-alias rights or ASYNC policy,
and no measured latency/frequency result is promised. Cancel/close, missing ACK,
loss, reset and S3 use the same retained GPU graph and terminal/full-reset receipts;
old claimed epochs cannot replay. No new hardware actor or automatic live policy
mutation is introduced.

#### Immutable legacy SSEU defaults

CONTEXT_PARAM_SSEU GET follows the 32-byte Linux context wire structure.
Size zero returns 32 without accessing the payload; a short size is EINVAL.
Lookup finalizes proto-contexts even for size queries. Legacy RENDER0/COPY0
selectors remain available. Nonindexed VIDEO/VIDEO_ENHANCE additionally resolve
only actually published Gen12 main-GuC engines by dense logical class/instance,
including sparse physical fuses. Indexed maps retain holes/bounds and ignore
engine_class as Linux does. All successful lookups copy the same immutable
whole-device default; they do not invent a per-media/codec SSEU allocation.
Flags and reserved fields are checked.
The old context ABI exposes only the low eight DSS bits and architecture EU
maximum (16 SIMD8 or eight SIMD16 units), not a reconfiguration or the full
fuse mask. Query blobs remain the full-width discovery interface. Copy faults
return EFAULT without publishing a new size; no namespace IRQ lock spans
faultable copies. SSEU SET is ENODEV on these >=Gen12 profiles (EINVAL for a
short structure), matching Linux's Gen11-only configuration support.

The private legacy-media lookup inventory is captured once per context from a
matching nonzero current Gen12 publication at an SSEU GET (including size-only)
or actual legacy media selection. Its host-only platform/EngineSet snapshot
survives stop/loss/reset without MMIO, wake acquisition, GPU allocation or an
execution grant. Creation alone does not capture it. A context that never
observed a qualified inventory returns ENODEV for media lookup while unavailable;
a known absent logical engine returns EINVAL. Later valid publication may seed
an absent snapshot. Existing RENDER0/COPY0 and retained indexed lookups remain
usable while stopped. Fresh submissions still independently require current
live admission and never use the query snapshot.

`drm_registry::driver_name` recognizes `intel-gpu` so both primary and render
nodes reach Intel dispatch and retain their GEM mmap/PRIME namespaces.
`drm_registry::card(index)` retains that card's Arc; DeviceInfo reads driver state
after the registry lock is released. `DeviceInfo::for_card` validates the
driver/vendor and exact integrated/Alchemist/Battlemage PCI profile and captures
that instance's optional immutable HWCONFIG and topology Arcs. Discrete profiles report system
RAM as system RAM; no local-memory region or Arc display binding is inferred.

`intel_gpu_exec::ExecRequest::read` admits a bounded softpin/no-relocation
residency plan: this file's unique handles, valid canonical GPU addresses,
alignment, non-overlap, first/last batch selection and in-object batch extent.
Both entry points follow i915_gem_execbuffer2_ioctl/i915_gem_do_execbuffer:
check_buffer_count and i915_gem_check_execbuffer (EINVAL: no buffers, illegal
flags, DRI1 cliprects without FENCE_ARRAY/USE_EXTENSIONS, DR1, DR4 other than
UXA's 0xffffffff, batch start/length alignment), then the exec-object copy
(EFAULT), then SECURE (ENODEV); IS_PINNED is accepted and rsvd1's upper half
ignored. Relocations, more than 4096 objects and, on the synchronous path,
fence flags are refused (EINVAL) with the header checks. rsvd2 is read only
for FENCE_IN/SUBMIT/OUT; otherwise any value is ignored.
`read_submission` then copies explicit synchronization once, and only after
it resolves the objects (eb_lookup_vmas);
`address_space(format, pat_index)` constructs immutable private PPGTT
tables retaining every referenced object; failed construction tears down all
tables. This compatibility planner has a single WB host PAT: WC and VRAM
objects shared from Xe refuse before admission. VM-associated native BOs also
refuse: their unique Xe VM restriction cannot be bypassed by private softpin
tables. The WB-only compatibility
MMAP_OFFSET and GET/SET_CACHING commands also refuse those native placements
rather than claiming WB or successful retyping; Xe's mapping interface remains
available. Shared WB handles, reservations and sync objects retain their
existing identity across the exact-command ABI dispatcher. An existing
VM/engine is never changed by admission. The plan's WRITE
bit selects writable leaves in this restricted path. Async EXECBUFFER2 and its
WR encoding copy the complete plan once, retain the per-open context, serialize
same-context callers with an async Mutex and await the prior context fence.
They wait for conflicting reservations only for entries requiring implicit
synchronization, then submit to this card's live GT backend with the copied
per-object policy and generation-checked synchronous final admission. Retry
after reservation/queue contention reuses the copied request; a queued job is
never replayed. Dropping a waiter, context handle, GEM handle or fd does not
cancel hardware ownership. Synchronous kernel dispatch returns WouldBlock for
a live backend; it cannot bridge a wait that depends on the GT worker.

The userspace path accepts EXEC_FENCE_IN/OUT/SUBMIT, EXEC_FENCE_ARRAY, and the
TIMELINE_FENCES extension through EXEC_USE_EXTENSIONS. FENCE_IN resolves this
process's sync_file fd (low32 of rsvd2); invalid/non-sync-file fds return EINVAL.
FENCE_SUBMIT uses the same fd field and is mutually exclusive with FENCE_IN.
It waits for each native Intel leaf's scheduling-enable acknowledgement,
without waiting for its terminal breadcrumb/retirement. Foreign leaves still
require completion. A terminal reset also satisfies the submit dependency,
including when enable was never acknowledged. The default
DrmFence::is_submit_ready is terminal readiness; only the native Intel fence
opts into the earlier milestone, preserved through syncobj/sync_file adapters.
Registration, policy and CT enqueue alone do not publish submit readiness.
FENCE_OUT may accompany either input mode and still exports a terminal fence.
GEM reservations, same-context ordering, binary/timeline WAIT and ordinary
fence polling/waits retain their completion requirements. Submit readiness
never releases resources or proves CPU visibility. Loss before acknowledgement
keeps the dependency pending until proven full reset; failure alone cannot
release uncertain GPU ownership.
Every input leaf and syncobj payload is retained before waiting, so close,
destroy, replacement or user-memory edits cannot retarget a pending request.
Each render open owns an independent SyncObjTable and routes the common DRM
binary/timeline create/destroy/wait/signal/fd/query/transfer ioctls to it.
Binary arrays use num_cliprects entries of {handle:u32, flags:u32}; WAIT=1,
SIGNAL=2. Timeline extensions use the 32-byte i915 base, count:u64,
handles_ptr:u64 and values_ptr:u64. Arrays and extensions are mutually
exclusive; flags, reserved fields, unknown extensions and same-point
timeline WAIT|SIGNAL fail before publication. A cycle is walked to the 513th
link (E2BIG), as is any longer chain. Each array follows
add_fence_array/add_timeline_fence_array: the overflow bound (EINVAL), access_ok
of each user array (EFAULT unless `ptr + size` neither wraps nor exceeds Linux's
USER_PTR_MAX: `(1 << 47) - 4096` on x86_64, TASK_SIZE_MAX `1 << 48` on
aarch64) and the eb->fences krealloc (ENOMEM once more than
KMALLOC_MAX_SIZE/32 = 131072 entries are added across the request; skipped
timeline entries do not count) precede the entries. Each entry is then copied
(EFAULT), flag-checked (EINVAL), its point read (EFAULT), its syncobj found
(ENOENT), retained and its fence resolved (EINVAL: WAIT with no fence, an
unfound point without SIGNAL, then same-point WAIT|SIGNAL) before the next is
copied. The IN/SUBMIT sync_file and its checks follow both arrays. There is no
other fence or dependency count bound; NARF allocation failure is ENOMEM.
Existing timeline payloads preserve
ordering, including when a SIGNAL point has not yet been submitted.
Explicit waits use timer awaits without holding IRQ-safe locks or restarting
a copied ioctl. After admission, output syncobjs reference the exact terminal
job fence, with binary replacement or timeline chain publication; retained
object Arcs survive handle destruction. Software syncobj signal cannot signal
the underlying hardware job.

`UserBackend::submit_with_output` and
`GuCGt::submit_user_batch_with_output` use a borrowed `UserOutput` transaction.
After allocation, reservation and cache publication succeed, install_sync_file
reserves an O_CLOEXEC descriptor, reports it in high32 of rsvd2 while preserving
low32, and installs the exact CompletionFence. Only then does the GT perform
its non-failing enqueue, with no await between fd installation and publication.
Descriptor exhaustion returns EMFILE; copyout/install failure rolls back the
context claim and all backing/reservations without queueing work or installing
a descriptor. No failed output transaction consumes a GuC ID or request stamp.
Reset completion is terminal for the exported fence; dropping/closing an
output fd cannot abandon hardware ownership.

`intel_gpu_user::UserBackend::huc_version` adds an object-safe async
`FsFuture<'_, (u8, u8, u8)>` hook whose default returns NoDevice. The retained
physical runtime overrides it under the async reset mutex and current epoch,
D0, forcewake and live authentication checks. On MTL/Arrow it answers through
`intel_gpu_gt::media::query_huc` from the published media GuC under GT1's
epoch, never GT0. Unqualified backends gain no
positive reply; this hook cannot load, authenticate, wake or resume firmware.

`intel_gpu_user::UserBackend` exposes a live `UserStatus` and async `submit`:
Err guarantees no job was queued; Ok returns the GT's terminal fence and
transfers residency regardless of caller lifetime. `ExecRequest::prepare_user`
constructs a `UserBatch` with private immutable PPGTT tables retaining its BOs.
`GuCGt::submit_user_batch` is the safe untrusted-command entry; the context's
immutable `Engine` selects an admitted render, copy or compute engine. All use
MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START bit8 (nonsecure PPGTT), independently of LRC descriptor
bit8 (PPGTT mode). Copy submission
follows xe_ring_ops.c's simple job: a TLB-invalidating MI_FLUSH_DW start
stamp, the batch, MI_ARB disable, an optional MI_FLUSH_DW plus posted PPGTT
user-fence store, then the owned MI_FLUSH_DW GGTT breadcrumb and
MI_USER_INTERRUPT. Kernel ring, HWS, LRC and page tables are absent from user
PPGTT/CPU mappings. Hardware command privilege checking and the reverified RCS
register whitelist apply throughout nested batches and concurrent CPU changes
to leaf BOs. Leaf mappings are untrusted; no software opcode whitelist or GPU
NX bit is claimed. Secure dispatch is always refused.

`GuCScheduler::submit_trusted_on_user_context` is the trusted-words-on-user-context entry point: it claims a bound `UserContext` and submits trusted MI_LRI words as a prefix-only job on that context, so per-context OA programming retires on the bound exec queue (Linux submits its LRI on `stream->exec_q`). The words carry the same trust contract as `submit_commands` — they must not alter GGTT or PPGTT page tables, rings, access policy, another context's saved state, or completion evidence — and the caller must have validated the binding first. Width-one contexts only; parallel contexts are refused, since prefix-only submissions cannot serve parallel lanes. `Gt::submit_oa_job` routes per-context OA jobs (`Job::per_context`) through this entry point and re-validates the binding at submit time, so a queue that died between `begin` and the submit fails with ENOENT instead of retiring on a gone queue; a per-context job never falls back to the kernel ring. Configuration jobs keep the kernel-ring path through `submit_commands`.

`UserContext` retains a private saved LRC body between jobs, sized and
header-checked for its engine (copy: one engine-state page; gen12_xcs layout
before Xe2, xe2_bcs on BMG). First execution starts from that engine's primed
golden image; later executions restore that context's
own saved state and overwrite ring/control/status/root fields with fresh owned
values. Capture synchronizes device writes only after exact head/breadcrumb,
deregistration and final TLB proof. Global saved-image storage is capped at
64 MiB. Allocation/cache/admission failure before publication rolls back the
context claim. Capture failure retains the entire job until full reset.
Pending jobs retain the context Arc. A proven reset bans affected contexts;
all contexts bound to an earlier GT epoch refuse reuse after rebuild. New
contexts can use the new epoch. User batches are not automatically replayed.

`ExecRequest::prepare(format, pat_index)` produces a `ResidentBatch` retaining
its private tables, BOs and arbitrary batch VA/extent. The internal Gen12
`RcsEngine::submit_resident` consumes this owner on an idle render context and
returns a request ID plus `CompletionFence`. Resident admission refuses queued
work as well as loaded work; root attach/detach also refuse queued work. The
submitted root and all leaf objects stay pinned across fd/handle close,
preemption and wait cancellation. A completed resident context's image root
is cleared before releasing its page tables.

`ExecRequest::prepare_for_gt(platform)` selects the physical GT's established
system-memory WB PAT for leaves: MTL/Arrow uses 3, DG2 uses 0 and BMG uses 2.
MTL/Arrow non-leaf entries and PDP0/PTBP use the separately installed UC PAT2;
DG2 and BMG use their WB policy for non-leaves too. `Ppgtt::with_table_pat` admits only the two-bit
non-leaf PAT field; `root_descriptor` includes PRESENT|RW and PAT, independently
of the raw root physical address. Invalid policy fails before allocation.
The immutable table pages and all resident BOs are explicitly cache-cleaned
before hardware publication, including the legacy Gen12 resident path. This
is required for Xe-LPG's non-snooping page-table reads. The CPU must not modify
published pages until terminal completion; one-time cleaning is not live
coherence for mutable tables.

Gen12 render breadcrumbs drain HDC, tile, render, depth and data caches with
CS/depth stalls, then publish a separate GGTT QW post-sync breadcrumb. XCS uses
MI_FLUSH_DW instead of render-only PIPE_CONTROL. Ring tails stay qword aligned;
wrap admission accounts for NOOP padding before writing. CSB publication uses
hardware release/acquire barriers. Retirement requires the active context's
exact final breadcrumb and saved head at the submitted tail. Missing proof
quarantines the engine (`CompletionLost`), refuses further submission and
leaves fences pending. CSB software identities are not reused within an engine
lifetime, including after slot reuse. The unsafe `release_after_reset` consumes
the engine only after its GT owner proves all DMA agents stopped; outstanding
fences then report `JobError::Reset`. Dropping an owner is not reset proof and
deliberately retains published resident address spaces. `CompletionFence::wait`
registers wakers; dropping that future removes only its waiter. First terminal
result wins. This internal primitive is not yet a published DRM sync-file API.
`wait_seqno_async` samples completion through timer awaits; the sync wrapper
uses `block_on_spin` for lock/IRQ callers outside executor polls. Neither wait
owns or cancels the request's residency.

`SubmissionProfile::for_generation` selects `Gen12GuC` for Tiger/Alder/
Raptor Lake and the separate Xe-LPG GuC path for Meteor/Arrow Lake. This
legacy generation-only selector refuses LNL/PTL; their native execution
requires the exact PCI/GMD/firmware and headless owner described below.
Existing default legacy RCS/media attach paths admit only Gen12 before MMIO.
A display gate cannot admit a render engine. The physical GuC path starts
owned contexts on exact Gen12, MTL/Arrow, DG2/BMG and qualified headless
LNL/PTL profiles. Separate media GTs, broader storage/PRIME integration and
Mesa acceptance remain outstanding. Graphics APIs and shader/state
generation belong in userspace.

`intel_gpu_gtt::PteFormat` distinguishes Gen12 and Xe-LPG GPU encodings:
PPGTT PAT[2:0] occupy bits 7,4,3; Xe-LPG adds PAT3 at bit62. Gen12 system GGTT
entries have no PAT bits; Xe-LPG GGTT PAT[1:0] occupy bits53:52. Intermediate
PPGTT entries carry PRESENT|RW and PAT[1:0] in bits4:3. There is no CPU-style NX/LRU encoding. The
common supported physical field is bits45:12, with 4-KiB system pages only.
`encode_engine_pte` and `Ppgtt::map` now take **writable**, replacing the previous
incorrect executable/NX contract. `Ppgtt::with_format`/`map_with_pat` expose
the generation and full PAT index; the GT owner establishes each PAT policy.
`alloc_contiguous_scanout_with_format` accepts an explicit GGTT format/index.
The Gen12 wrappers use its PAT-free GGTT encoding. Context attachment writes
the raw PML4 physical address to PDP0, leaving PDP1–3 zero.
The Gen12 context codec uses engine-relative LRI selectors, thirteen initial
register pairs, the extended render restore groups and an RCS terminator at
dword 0xb9 (XCS at 0x34). RING_CTL encodes bytes minus one page in bits20:12;
the Gen11/Gen12 CSB has twelve entries. These register-model corrections do
not establish a fully initialized, isolated or recoverable userspace engine.

`intel_gpu_guc::CssImage::parse` validates CSS, uCode and RSA component ranges,
required firmware major version, optional complete/truncated key suffix and
bounded private-data size. It preserves separate release (CSS byte 64) and
submission-interface (byte 68) versions; scheduling requires interface major 1
and rejects unknown/unsupported interfaces before engine publication. Parsing
grants no asset authority or signature validity.
`CtSender`/`CtReceiver` operate through `CtMemory` over coherent shared memory:
host/GuC own distinct head/tail fields, with hardware release/acquire barriers
on every publication. Requests have bounded HXG lengths and source-defined
wire headers. Full buffers leave memory unchanged. Invalid descriptor status,
foreign cursor modification, malformed/truncated messages or invalid origin
poison the owner without advancing a receive head or releasing pending work.
The platform owner must retain CT memory until confirmed deregistration/reset;
these primitives do not load/authenticate firmware, register transport or wake
an engine. Fixtures pin CSS/CTB wire cases and ownership failure behavior.

`intel_gpu_guc_firmware::GuCFirmware::open` accepts Meteor/Arrow Lake and an
existing `Cap<FirmwareRegistry, Read>`. Both registry open and immutable blob
copy run through `Cap::invoke`. It selects `i915/mtl_guc_70.bin`, bounds and
validates CSS before copying, requires the selected 70.53.0-or-newer ABI-70
baseline and a 384-byte RSA signature, and retains the registry digest/signer.
No ambient firmware authority or direct filesystem access is introduced.
Registry authorization does not establish GuC boot-ROM authentication.

`intel_gpu_gt::GtPlatform::from_pci` separates integrated display generation
from GT identity: the canonical integrated table plus exact Linux DG2 (25)
and BMG (13) PCI IDs. `guc()` selects MTL/Arrow, Alchemist or Battlemage's
firmware profile; other generations have no new GuC bootstrap profile.
Identity discovery alone neither registers an Arc display driver nor reports
system RAM as discrete GPU memory. `GuCFirmware::open_for_platform` uses the
same invoked-capability acquisition for `i915/dg2_guc_70.bin` (70.53.0+) and
`xe/bmg_guc_70.bin` (70.54.0+), retaining the selected platform with the bytes.

`intel_gpu_guc_boot::GuCBoot::stage` consumes a GT `BootAllocator`, an invoked-
authority firmware image and the actual PCI ID/revision, HuC upload extent and
already-programmed uncached MOCS index (required for BMG). It validates the
target, WOPCM fit, GGTT extents above the reserved 8-MiB WOPCM window and
non-overlapping allocations before MMIO;
partial allocation failure rolls back. The default three owned allocations
contain GuC CSS/uCode/RSA, minimal ADS plus firmware-private data, and logs.
Exact-TGL `stage_with_huc` adds a fourth owned HuC upload/RSA buffer, deriving
the pre-WOPCM reservation from the authorized image before either DMA pass.
`GuCBoot::stage_media` with a HuC (`intel_gpu_huc::Firmware` plus its adopt
flag) adds the same fourth buffer on the MTL/Arrow media GuC. It holds the
whole GSC-headered file; the DMA reads from its CSS offset and the RSA
pointer is the base plus xe_uc_fw_rsa_offset. All four participate in
rollback, pairwise/protected extents and cache sync. Other profiles retain
their original three allocations. Minimal
ADS uses the source-defined 16-class/32-instance layout with invalid mapping
value 32, zero enabled engines, valid policies and owned private-data pointers.
The log layout is one state page plus 16-KiB crash, 64-KiB event and 1-MiB
capture buffers. Scheduler and verbose logging are disabled during bootstrap.

`begin` and every active `poll` require GT forcewake acknowledged at the
platform-specific register: DG2 uses 0x130044, while MTL/Arrow and BMG use
0xdfc (`xe_force_wake_init_gt`, graphics IP 12.70+). The sole GT owner
holds forcewake/runtime-PM and serializes reset and firmware DMA across the
entire operation. The state machine issues GuC-domain reset, requires reset
self-clear **and** MIA-in-reset status, validates prelocked WOPCM or programs
and verifies its write-once registers, publishes scratch parameters and cache-
cleaned memory, selects generation-correct GuC TLB invalidation, then starts
CSS+uCode DMA to WOPCM offset 0x2000 with the RSA GGTT pointer separate. Default
WOPCM is 2 MiB on Gen12 and qualified headless LNL/PTL, and 4 MiB on
MTL/Arrow and admitted discrete profiles, with a 36 KiB hardware-context
reservation. A prelocked layout is validated against the source's 8-MiB bound. BMG uses MOCS and the DESC1/DESC0
TLB sequence. Reset, DMA and authentication have bounded deadlines; `wait`
uses timer awaits. DMA completion precedes authentication; only non-reset
READY plus good hardware authentication establishes `BootState::Ready`.
Boot-ROM/uKernel errors, unreadable registers, wake loss and timeout stop
admission and retain all resources. Dropping a waiter cannot release the
owning buffers. Unexposed staged owners reclaim memory on drop. Without HuC
exposure, the existing GuC bootstrap stop requires GuC reset and independent
firmware DMA idle. An exposed HuC graph is different: sticky exposure survives
reload and failed re-begin, so neither BootStaged nor BootStopped permits its
reclamation. The enclosing full Gen12 engine reset and retained media ACK
retirement, or an explicit unsafe full HuC/media-stop proof, must complete
before physical release. GuC-only reset/DMA idle is insufficient for HuC and
does not prove completion/reset of RCS jobs. Newer profiles keep their existing
mapping-retirement and wake-release ordering. The media GuC's HuC object is
read only by its DMA and the media GuC's AUTHENTICATE_HUC, so a verified media
GuC stop reclaims it. On the media GuC the HuC DMA precedes only the
submission load, a set auth bit never refuses the upload, and a locked WOPCM
that cannot host the HuC skips it instead of refusing the boot.

`BootAllocator::sync_for_device` is mandatory before DMA. The SharedArena
adapter cleans every owned CPU cache line through existing architecture
primitives, with compiler and hardware fences; cache cleaning does not prove
concurrent CT coherence. `GpuBacking::coherent_for_device` defaults false.
`allocate_transport` requires authenticated boot and clones the shared arena/
MMIO owner into the CT transport; discrete transport construction additionally
requires a backing that explicitly guarantees coherent shared cache lines.
Legacy FrameBacking makes no coherence claim. The physical-GT arena below
admits x86_64 system memory only after installing its platform PAT/MOCS policy;
Linux's DG2/BMG system-memory contract is CPU-coherent. ARM PCI host-bridge
coherence is unproven and physical scheduling refuses that backing. Local VRAM
allocation and complete engine/media/cache inventory remain separate work.

`intel_gpu_guc_gt::GuCGt::stage` owns the staged firmware bootstrap and its
optional CT transport together. It is an exclusive graphics-GT owner, not a
second reference counter over the legacy Gen12 forcewake manager. The PCI
owner must supply runtime-PM, physical-function admission and serialization
with every other GT reset/firmware user. `begin` refuses an existing kernel
request or stale kernel ACK, then sets only kernel request bit 0 at 0xa188
using masked writes; other requestors' bits survive. `poll` waits for the
selected ACK before starting GuC reset/DMA. Wake and sleep transitions have
50-ms deadlines; `wait` cooperatively yields and uses timer awaits. Cancellation leaves the state,
request and allocations owned by the GT.

After authenticated `Ready`, `begin_ct` allocates and enables one owned CT;
neither bootstrap nor transport escapes the owner. Discrete coherence or
allocation refusal leaves the GuC ready for explicit stop. `send`/`receive`
require `CtReady` and validate both the kernel request and ACK. CT ring full
and malformed host messages are recoverable; corrupt device cursors, mailbox
errors and wake loss stop admission. Unreadable registers never prove sleep
or stop. `begin_stop` closes admission first, reasserts a lost wake request
when registers remain readable, then resets GuC and requires MIA-in-reset
plus firmware DMA idle. Only that proof retires even partial/poisoned CT
registrations. It then clears the kernel request and awaits ACK deassertion.
The stopped owner is terminal; no stale child can restart CT. For minimal
bootstrap/CT owners this proof covers only GuC allocations. A physical owner
with a scheduler additionally requires the full-engine reset described below
before releasing contexts or CT.

Drop frees only unpublished or fully stopped GT owners. All other states
retain the entire allocator/MMIO/bootstrap/CT object graph, preserving the
wake request while DMA lifetime is uncertain. `release_after_gt_reset` is an
unsafe escape requiring the PCI owner's external full-reset proof covering
all owned DMA addresses, engine HWS/LRC references and both graphics-GT and
render-well kernel wake requests. This owner does not publish userspace engines
or enable EXECBUFFER2.

`GuCGt::stage_hardware` composes the minimal owner with render-well startup and
an owned kernel scheduler. `start_hardware().await` performs wake, bootstrap,
optional source-supported HWCONFIG, scheduling reload and CT enablement; cancellation retains the whole
transaction with its caller. `intel_gpu_gt_hw::AuthorizedWindow` invokes the
PCI write capability for every bounded, aligned BAR access. Revocation yields
unavailable reads and closes admission. A per-function `GgttArena::for_gt`
reserves CPU frames and GGTT addresses without publishing PTEs until hardware
initialization succeeds. The physical owner acquires render kernel wake at
0xa278/ACK 0xd84, proves inherited GuC reset plus DMA idle, then completes
GRDOM_FULL before changing cache policy or publishing new mappings.

The owned system-memory policies are MTL PAT3=2, DG2 PAT0=3 and BMG PAT2=0xf,
with their source-defined MOCS/LNCF tables. MTL additionally installs UC PAT2=0xc
for non-leaf PPGTT reads, and leaves inherited display PAT0
unchanged. MCR multicast writes preserve the selector and use the hardware
steering semaphore where required; no await occurs while holding it. Only
successful installation creates `CachePolicy`, which authorizes staged PTEs
and coherent x86_64 backing. `BootAllocator::configure_cache` defaults to
refusal and applies that proof to each staged backing before publication.
BMG GGTT writes include Wa_22019338487's G-unit
drain. GuC host and RCS interrupts stay masked during startup. Once execution
probes pass, the physical service attempts owned MSI delivery as described
below. Wake/reset/semaphore waits have
deadlines and async timer/yield progression.

Before firmware DMA, `GuCBoot::begin` validates and binds two matching live
GMD samples to the admitted Xe-LPG/Battlemage IP and stepping; DG2 uses its
pre-GMD identity. Unsupported, unavailable or unstable observations return
`BootError::Graphics`; a changed supported identity refuses reload. Both
initial discovery and scheduling reload publish source-defined GuC WA flags
and zero-payload 16:16 ADS KLVs before cache synchronization. The KLV page at
ADS+0x3000 is separate from engine saves/private data, with the complete
64-bit pointer and byte size in the packed ADS ABI. DG2 G11 selects context
isolation, Xe-LPG pre-B0 selects hold-switchout, and Battlemage 20.01/20.02
select different KLV lists. RCS0, BCS0, BMG BCS8 and selected compute engines follow the
discovered engine set. Firmware flags do not grant
userspace isolation, coordinated reset or RC6 admission.

`GuCGt::begin_scheduling` requires awake authenticated Ready, validated HWCONFIG,
observed nonempty geometry DSS, supported submission ABI and no CT. A compute-only
GT cannot authorize RCS0 programming or allocation. It allocates owned HWS and golden-LRC
storage for each admitted engine (`intel_gpu_engine::Engine::ALL`), enters
`PreparingScheduling`, and applies graphics-GT/RCS0 MMIO
workarounds and tunings before enabling the ring. `intel_gpu_gt_registers`
selects exact DG2 G10/G11/G12 IDs, Xe-LPG 12.70/12.71/12.74 with pre-B0
differences, and Battlemage 20.01/20.02 with flat-CCS and DSS-group fuse rules.
Ordinary registers preserve unrelated bits; masked writes use hardware masks.
Reads target live DSS/L3/MSLICE instances, DG2 implicit targets, or the
source-defined modern instance zero. Modern firmware steering contention
yields with a deadline; every acquired semaphore is released and the selector
restored on success or error. Preflight refuses unavailable registers before
WA writes; readback failures close admission and retain owned storage through
full reset. DG2 CACHE_MODE_SS is not read back (Wa_14012342262). BMG also
receives each BCS engine's ENGINE_BASE copies of Wa_16021639441/priority-read
(CSFE_CHICKEN1 0x220d4 / 0x3ee0d4) and Wa_16023105232
(RING_PSMI_CTL 0x22050 / 0x3ee050).

BMG's architecture-present BCS8 uses hardware base 0x3ee000 and physical
instance eight, with its own two-page copy LRC, HWS, golden image and private
PPGTT startup store probe. ADS enables physical COPY bits 0 and 8 (0x101),
maps logical COPY1 to physical eight, and records separate instance register
saves. CT scheduling selects it with logical submit mask two. No epoch is
published until its probe retires and validates. Native Xe and explicit i915
engine maps can select COPY1; the legacy BLT selector continues to mean BCS0.
Linux reserves the highest BCS for USM. NARF has no USM owner and currently
admits ordinary copy jobs there; adding USM must reserve/revoke that engine's
userspace availability rather than silently sharing its ownership.

**Boot-selected compute partition.** `narf.intel.ccs_mode=N` initially selects one
through four compute engines on DG2/BMG; absence means one. Exactly one
canonical value is accepted before the boot `--` delimiter. Bare, duplicate,
malformed and out-of-range settings return `RuntimeError::Configuration`
before startup. Integrated profiles require one. The requested count must not
exceed and must divide the physical fused compute-slice count; invalid
selections refuse scheduling rather than silently changing the request.

`GuCGt::begin_scheduling_with_ccs_mode(now, N)` freezes the physical fuse mask,
selected engines and partition. Existing `begin_scheduling` delegates to one.
Only present slices are assigned in source order, round-robin over the first N
present physical CCS engines; absent slices stay disabled. RCU_MODE and
CCS_MODE writes are verified and later scheduling-policy checks require the
same partition without live repair. `Engine` names physical identity;
`EngineSet::logical_instance` and `from_class_instance` exclusively convert
dense user instances. Each engine has independent saves/default priming,
nonprivileged policy, IRQ attribution, timestamps, watchdog and PPGTT proof.
Full reset/S3 requires revalidation. Clean runtime resume may retain a user
epoch only when the exact physical EngineSet, raw fuse mask and requested
mode match the parked state. The partition is never patched on live engines;
dynamic changes require the client-free reset transaction below.

**Client-free compute reconfiguration.** DG2/BMG card sysfs exposes cached
`ccs_mode`, read-only `num_cslices` and `ccs_mode_status`. A current
initial-namespace CAP_SYS_ADMIN grant is required for every mode store.
The bounded scalar accepts canonical 1..4, subject to the same fuse/divisor
rules. Stores enqueue one request and perform no MMIO or waits. Status
distinguishes unavailable, ready, queued, applying, applied and failed;
acceptance is asynchronous and does not claim Linux's synchronous sysfs reset
semantics. The scalar remains the last confirmed configuration during loss.

Both primary and render node construction acquire a per-card client lease
before namespaces or master side effects, including before backend readiness
and on GT-only cards without a mode-state `Card`. The lease outlives namespace
destruction and the last `Arc` of its file. Request acceptance atomically
requires zero clients and closes the same gate. New devfs lookups temporarily
return no file while that gate is closed; directory enumeration may still list
the nodes. Other vendors and invalid indices create no Intel gate.

The worker first takes a runtime-PM reference outside the GT mutex. Under
that mutex it requires the exact old epoch/partition and an idle `GuCGt`,
including jobs retained after lastclose. Busy work refuses the change without
reset. Otherwise it closes the public epoch, controls and IRQ delivery before
the existing GuC plus full-engine stop, and retains the gate and power through
fresh bring-up and every selected engine's startup proof. Only verified new
epoch publication reopens clients. True loss/S3 close retires the prior epoch
even without pending work; a stale callback cannot publish it again. Ordinary
idle park retains the same partition/epoch contract. Width-one load balancing
and bounded single-row width-two through width-four groups use that published
partition; multi-placement groups and GPU user-fence joins remain separate work.

`intel_gpu_nonpriv::EnginePolicy` initializes each admitted engine's twelve
FORCE_TO_NONPRIV slots while idle under the GT owner's forcewake holds.
Every inherited slot is cleared to its own RING_NOPID (including 0x3ee094
for BCS8) and verified before any grant is written; copy engines
have no whitelist entries on these profiles and retain NOPID in all twelve.
Unavailable slot reads refuse admission. Render/compute engines install the
address-sorted Linux Xe policy after verifying the deny fill: OAG status
read-only (0xdafc), four read-only registers from OA head (0xdb00), and MMIO
trigger read/write (0xdb1c). Nine unused entries retain the NOPID fill. Full-word
posted readback checks addresses, range, access, DENY and reserved bits; a
failed clear never publishes a new grant or enables the ring.
`GuCGt` verifies the complete policy again after scheduling firmware reload,
before publishing SchedulingReady at CT enablement, and before kernel probe,
default-context priming or resident batch admission. A failed verification
returns `GtError::Registers` and enters Lost without repairing live policy or
releasing DMA owners/reservations. GuC reset plus full-engine reset remains
required before terminal reset fences or reclamation. The policy covers only
the admitted Gen12, DG2, Xe-LPG12.70/12.71/12.74, BMG20.01/20.02 and exact
headless LNL/PTL engine profiles. Qualified main-GuC Gen12 VIDEO/ENHANCE
uses the source timestamp-only policy described below. The opt-in MTL/Arrow
standalone media GT uses its oam_mmio_trg_vcs/vecs table (see "Intel MTL/Arrow
standalone media GT opt-in"); legacy standalone execlists and other separate
media GTs require their own tables.
Installing OA register access alone does not open an OA stream or userspace queue.

This covers the graphics GT and its admitted RCS0, BCS0, BMG BCS8 and fused
compute engines, plus the fuse-present Gen12 main-GuC VIDEO/ENHANCE profile
described below. Separate media GTs remain refused except the opt-in MTL/Arrow
GT1 profile, which has its own media-only ADS. The
owner enables their rings under both wake holds and stops GuC before rewriting
ADS. The reload enables RCS0 (GuC class 0), copy (class 3) and compute (class 4),
installing their mapping/enable masks, per-engine HWS/register saves
(RING_MODE, HWS_PGA, IMR),
golden LRCA and source-defined post-register state sizes, selects LiteRestore and disables autonomous
engine resets until coordinated recovery is implemented. Firmware is then uploaded
and authenticated again; ADS is never rewritten while live. GuC GGTT TLB
invalidation precedes CT registration. `SchedulingReady` gives the scheduler
exclusive CT receive ownership; raw `send`/`receive` remain limited to CtReady.

`intel_gpu_guc_sched::GuCScheduler` admits at most 64 independent resident/probe
contexts, each with its own coherent 8-KiB ring and engine-sized LRC: render
uses 14 pages on MTL/DG2 or four on BMG, copy uses two pages, and compute uses
14 pages on MTL/DG2 or three on BMG. Literal register-state groups follow the
platform's Xe LRC layout.
`GuCGt::submit_kernel_probe` and async `intel_gpu_gt_runtime::kernel_probe(card)`
return a completion fence for a fixed owned command stream that writes its
request stamp to its own breadcrumb. They accept no user GPU instructions or
external addresses. A round-robin pool reuses GuC IDs 1..64 only after
disable/deregister, exact head/breadcrumb and final TLB acknowledgement; all
unretired IDs remain leased, including during failed cleanup. Priming retains
the seed's ID until the different switch context retires and capture succeeds.
There is no lifetime request-count limit. Independent nonzero 31-bit stamps
identify requests; pre-invalidation cookies carry the stamp and retirement
cookies add bit31. On wrap, every live stamp is skipped. Breadcrumbs compare
the request stamp rather than the recyclable context ID. Old generation-bearing
TLB ACKs and breadcrumbs close admission without completing a replacement job.
Full-width cookies follow `intel_guc_submission.c::guc_send_invalidate_tlb`'s
32-bit lookup allocation; no context-ID bits are interpreted as a generation.
Scheduling/deregister responses carry only the ID: reuse depends on GuC's
deregistration contract (as in Xe), which ends the old context's messages.
The final TLB ACK additionally proves our backing reclamation barrier.

`GuCGt::submit_kernel_batch` consumes a `ResidentBatch` prepared for that exact
GT profile. This is an unsafe trusted-kernel interface: all instructions and
nested batches must be trusted, access only resident mappings, return with
BB_END and leave global/transport/context/ring state and completion evidence
untouched, with no CPU/user/peer writes to any resident
BO before terminal completion. It does not establish userspace 3D state or
isolation. Each context retains its private tables and objects through stop,
waiter cancellation and failures. Registration selects PPGTT (descriptor bit8),
PDP0/PTBP receives the full root descriptor, and MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START selects
PPGTT. The ring brackets execution with preparser/TLB/cache invalidation,
MTL AuxCCS invalidation and DG2/Xe-LPG's extra depth flush as applicable, and a full
render-cache drain before the separate GGTT post-sync breadcrumb. Retirement
checks the submitted tail, not a fixed probe size; all residency is dropped
before the terminal fence is signalled.

`GuCGt::submit_ppgtt_probe` and async `kernel_ppgtt_probe(card)` construct a
fixed store batch with private, unexported read-only code and writable result
BOs at separate 48-bit GPU addresses. `PpgttProbeSubmission` returns its context
ID, completion fence and read-only `PpgttProbeResult`; `verify()` checks the
entire result and unchanged code pages after successful completion. Physical
startup requires the original GGTT probe, context priming below, and one
private PPGTT probe on every advertised physical engine to retire and validate
before publishing userspace readiness. Failure retains uncertain ownership
and cannot publish a partial engine set.

`GuCGt::begin_context_defaults(now)` requires an awake SchedulingReady GT with
no pending contexts, no prior resident work and no existing default image.
Only the fixed GGTT probe can precede priming on a fresh GT. It returns an owned fence;
the caller/worker must continue `poll` until that fence completes. During
priming, external submission returns Busy. `intel_gpu_context` selects the
source-defined RCS context workarounds and tunings for DG2, Xe-LPG graphics
12.70/12.71/12.74 and Battlemage 20.01/20.02. Modern GMD ID, L3 and preemption
fuses require matching available samples. DSS steering uses observed live
units and HWCONFIG layout maxima (the source's four-DSS fallback for absent
maxima); L3 steering selects a live bank. Masked writes preserve unrelated
bits; non-masked tuning uses steered GPU MI_MATH read/modify/write and clears
its GPRs and selective-read selector afterward. Wa_14019789679 explicitly
seeds all fifty SVG commands with zero payloads on its source-qualified IP
range through graphics20.04; PTL graphics30.00/30.01 does not emit those
commands. Gen12 retains its source zero-SVG layout. Xe2 uses
DRAWING_RECTANGLE_FAST in place of
DG2/Xe-LPG's non-pipelined DRAWING_RECTANGLE. This table covers context state,
not global GT/engine initialization.

The priming scheduler fully retires the seed context while retaining its
image, then executes and fully retires a different context to force a save.
Only afterward does it synchronize the seed image for CPU access, copy the
opaque device-saved body into the owned golden image, clear status/ring/root
identity, and synchronize the template for GPU reads. Engines prime in
`Engine::ALL` order: after RCS0 publishes, BCS0 seeds xe_gt.c's emit_wa_job
equivalent (a non-MCR MI_MATH RMW of BLIT_CCTL to the platform's uncached MOCS
index, then GPR clear), switches and publishes its own one-page golden image,
with admission still Busy. Only the last engine's publication
sets `context_defaults_ready()` and signals the fence; cancellation releases
only waiters. New contexts copy this body, enable restoration, clear status
and assign their own ring, timestamp and PDP0/PTBP. Malformed save evidence,
allocation/synchronization failure, timeout or wake loss closes admission and
retains uncertain images until proven full reset. The normal stop/reset proof
also covers a retained seed and an in-flight switch context. Autoscheduled
engine resets remain disabled. Userspace publication additionally requires
the runtime's verified PPGTT probe and backend installation.

GuC power management follows xe_guc_pc_start. When scheduling becomes ready
and before the kernel probe, `GuCGt::begin_slpc` reads stable main-GT fused
RPn/RPe/RP0 limits and allocates an 8 KiB SLPC
shared buffer (coherent GGTT, no overlap with scheduler storage), zeroes it,
publishes its size and sends the fast request
HOST2GUC_PC_SLPC_REQUEST(SLPC_EVENT_RESET, address). Polling observes
`global_state` RUNNING (3) within 1005 ms, queries firmware defaults, clamps
them to the admitted limits and confirms the programmed range before sending
SETUP_PC_GUCRC (GUCRC_FIRMWARE_CONTROL). GuC owns GT frequency and RC6; the
host programs no RC6 registers. `intel_gpu_slpc` owns the bounded control
transaction and its separate CT fence namespace. `GuCGt::slpc_status` returns
confirmed `Limits`, `FrequencyRange` and `PowerProfile` only while SLPC is
Running. `begin_slpc_frequency_range` validates ordered MHz bounds, including
hardware rounding, and `begin_slpc_power_profile` selects Base or PowerSaving.
The owner must keep polling: enqueue is not acknowledgment, and Updating has
no publishable status. Range updates require a final firmware query matching
the requested rounded values. Invalid ranges leave the confirmed state intact;
firmware refusal, stale replies, malformed readback or timeout mark SLPC
Unavailable without closing scheduling. A refused start (allocation, cache,
CT) frees the buffer, which GuC never saw. Once sent, the buffer is retained
until proven reset, like all GuC-reachable storage.

The source-qualified conservative bounds retain BMG G21's 1200 MHz floor
(Wa_14022085890) and graphics IP 20.01's 2133 MHz MERT cap
(Wa_22019338487). Exact main-GT physical BMG graphics 20.01 also qualifies
Wa16023588340: production runtime must complete `prepare_mert` before public
execution/VRAM epochs and controls. A positively confirmed bootstrap cap and
actual frequency <=2133 MHz are required within 100 ms; unavailable SLPC refuses
this profile. Bounded MCR setup enables XE2_GAMREQSTRM_CTRL 0x4194 bit 6 while
preserving its unrelated fields and writes XEHPC_L3CLOS_MASK(3) 0xb1ac=0xf.
Selector state is preserved and semaphore ownership is bounded to 50 ms.
GLOBAL_INVAL 0xb404 must clear within 1 ms before an acknowledged SLPC transaction
restores the stashed initial range, clamped to fresh fused/G21 limits. Only
then does the writable ceiling expand to RP0. This profile uses the source
host-L2 invalidation path; other graphics versions, media and VF remain outside
this qualification.

BMG CPU-VRAM initialization retains the target BO and PM hold under the GT
owner before its first BAR write. A bounded lease admits one clear at a time;
cancellation abandons only the waiter. The GT poll owner drains complete or
abandoned partial clears through their own fresh, monotonically identified
global-flush ticket before release. Pending clears exclude idle. Raw 20.01
VRAM access also refuses before MERT preparation. Epoch, current PCI
D0/capability and wake are checked
before every new hardware access. No PCODE transaction is added.

On stop, existing GuC reset/DMA/full-engine proofs retire execution first.
`StoppingMert` independently retains firmware/wake while requesting at most
min(RPe,RP0,2133 MHz), settling at least 100 us, proving actual frequency within
100 ms, and completing a new global flush and verified host-L2 disable. Pending
CPU-clear targets survive execution reset until this separate proof. Failed
proof retains uncertain state, BOs and wake even if the lost GT is dropped,
and refuses wake release/D3/S3 handoff. Pending flush/promotion intent never
replays into a fresh owner; existing confirmed
SLPC user policy replays only after fresh qualification.

The opt-in MTL/Arrow media GuC (`narf.intel.media_gt=1`) runs the same owner
by role. `Limits::read_media` takes stable GT1 RPn/RP0 from
MTL_MEDIAP_STATE_CAP 0x138020 and RPe from MTL_MPE_FREQUENCY 0x13802c, with no
workaround cap. After the default LRCs and engine probes,
`GuCGt::begin_media_power` writes GT1's POWERGATE_ENABLE (0x38a210:
MEDIA_POWERGATE_ENABLE plus both VDN bits per present VCS) and starts SLPC.
The media start lowers only firmware defaults above RP0, confirms programmed
bounds by readback, then sends GUCRC_FIRMWARE_CONTROL, the compute strategy (a
refusal is ignored) and the Base profile. `MediaGuc` publishes GT1 only after
SLPC is Running, and any start failure stops GT1 (`MediaGucError::Slpc`), as
xe_uc_load_hw fails. `MediaGuc::slpc_status` reports the confirmed status
while GT1 is published, `MediaGuc::mc6_residency_ms` reads `MTL_MEDIA_MC6`
(`0x138048`, 1.28 us units) and `MediaGuc::act_freq_mhz` reads
`MTL_MIRROR_TARGET_WP1` (`0x380c60`, bits [8:0] in 16.67 MHz units). Before any reset of a GuC that started media power,
with wake held, the owner sends GUCRC_HOST_CONTROL if firmware control was
handed over, then writes RC_CONTROL, RC_STATE and POWERGATE_ENABLE to zero at
GT1's GSI copies. The main GT's sequence and stop are unchanged. Read-only
per-GT frequency and idle telemetry is exposed through `intel_gpu_gt_sysfs`
(`gt/`, `gt0/`, `device/tile0/gt0/{freq0,gtidle}/`) and
`intel_gpu_media_gt_sysfs` (`gt1/`, `device/tile0/gt1/{freq0,gtidle}/`);
writable per-card SLPC controls below remain GT0's.

`intel_gpu_power_controls::PowerControls` supplies a bounded per-card mailbox
through `UserBackend::power_controls`. The GT owner explicitly activates a
ready user epoch and closes admission before suspend, park or reset. Stores
never wait for firmware; one queued/in-flight request is permitted, and
further requests return Busy. The owner services native GuC controls under
its existing GT mutex. Confirmed values disappear during update and return
only after the native matched-reply/readback protocol completes. Failed
commands expose failure through `slpc_status`; unavailable clock values are
empty rather than fabricated zero.

Intel card sysfs nodes expose writable `gt_min_freq_mhz`, `gt_max_freq_mhz`,
`slpc_frequency_range` (two decimal MHz values), and `slpc_power_profile`
(`base` or `power-saving`). Read-only `gt_RPn_freq_mhz`, `gt_RP1_freq_mhz`,
`gt_RP0_freq_mhz` and `slpc_status` report confirmed limits and mailbox state.
The gt_* names follow i915; slpc_* files and asynchronous store acceptance
are NARF extensions, not the Xe freq0 sysfs ABI. Writable controls apply to
GT0 only, while read-only `tile0/gt0/{freq0,gtidle}` and
`tile0/gt1/{freq0,gtidle}` trees (`cur_freq`, `act_freq`, `min_freq`,
`max_freq`, `rp0_freq`, `rpe_freq`, `rpn_freq`, `power_profile`, `name`,
`idle_residency_ms`, `idle_status`, `gt1-mc`) plus `gt0/` and `gt1/`
telemetry attributes (`rps_*_freq_mhz`, `rc6*_residency_ms`, `slpc_status`,
`slpc_power_profile`) report GT0 and GT1 telemetry through `UserBackend`. Every writable SLPC callback requires
current initial-namespace CAP_SYS_ADMIN; reads remain cached. Only confirmed user policy survives
close; a newly activated GT revalidates it against fresh limits and replays
range then profile with acknowledgments. Queued/unacknowledged old-epoch
requests are discarded, and a stale worker observation cannot reopen a
closed mailbox.

`intel_gpu_hwmon::Monitor` registers a per-card cached `xe` hwmon node for
DG2/BMG, with a `device` link to that card's PCI device. The GT owner samples
at most once per second while Running, checking current PCI D0 and capability
authority before each read. Sysfs reads use only the owned cache; observations
older than two seconds, closed epochs and unavailable registers read empty,
never fabricated zero. Ready-epoch activation and park/reset/S3 closure use
the same GT mutex as SLPC. A stale sampling call cannot reopen a closed epoch.
Known admission/D0/authority denial immediately hides matching-epoch cached
sensor, fan, thermal-limit and power observations, including between sampling
ticks. Sampling timestamps retain the 1 Hz limit; fan recovery requires a new
baseline and energy continuity waits for fresh activation. Optional all-ones
registers remain field-local failures.

Names and units follow Xe hwmon: `temp2_input`/`temp2_label` are package
millidegrees/`pkg`, `temp3_*` aggregate VRAM/`vram`; BMG's sixteen individual
channels use `temp6_*` through `temp21_*` with `vram_ch_N` labels. Absent
individual channels read empty. DG2 adds `in1_input` in rounded millivolts and
`energy2_input` in microjoules, both labeled `pkg`. Energy extends the 32-bit
hardware counter across observed wrap using checked accumulation. Missing
authority/units/counter, changed units, overflow or a gap beyond two seconds
disables that energy series until a fresh activation; reset/resume starts a
new series. The retained owner also services a finite DG2/BMG extension
whitelist; sensor/fan sampling remains at most 1 Hz and sysfs performs no MMIO.

DG2 exposes package PL1 as CAP_SYS_ADMIN-gated `power2_max` (microWatts).
Stores queue a bounded current-epoch request; only the GT owner writes the
source-defined register, preserving unrelated/time-window fields. Nonzero
requests must fit SKU minimum/maximum and the original boot ceiling; no disable
or increase above that ceiling is admitted. The first valid enabled PL1
observation defines this card owner's boot ceiling. It survives close/resume
and is not replaced by our lowered setting. Unit/SKU/enabled state is
revalidated per epoch and pending requests are never replayed after
close/reset. Applied means exact posted register readback, not a firmware ACK;
non-sticking/locked hardware is Readback failure without a guessed lock bit.
Read-only `power2_rated_max`, `power2_max_default`, `power2_max_min`,
`power2_max_max` report observed limits. `power2_max_status` distinguishes
ready, queued, applying, applied and failed requests.
Missing/stale/closed/access-lost measurements read empty.

DG2 also exposes CAP_SYS_ADMIN-gated `power2_max_interval` in milliseconds,
with read-only `power2_max_interval_min`/`power2_max_interval_max`. Interval
and PL1 writes share one request slot and `power2_max_status`. The owner
freshly rechecks units, encodes the source's rounded 1.x*2^y time window,
updates only bits23:17 and requires exact whole-register readback. Power,
enable, clamp and all other fields are preserved. Nonzero requests and
represented intervals must fit the source's x0/y18 maximum (256000 ms only
with time-unit shift10). Sub-millisecond/zero representations refuse. Closing
discards queued requests; no pending interval is replayed after activation.

BMG additionally exposes the firmware-selected I1 threshold: `power1_crit`
(card microWatts) or `curr2_crit` (package milliamps). Potential attributes are
registered statically; incompatible/unavailable values and labels read empty,
and incompatible stores return Unsupported. Matching `power1_label`/`curr2_label`
and `*_crit_default`/`*_crit_min`/`*_crit_max` are read-only; `i1_status` reports
asynchronous outcomes. The first valid nonzero mode/threshold is retained as
a conservative ceiling, not a SKU guarantee. U10.6 values use nearest input
quantization; the minimum exported reading is 15625 microWatts or 15 mA.
Every store requires current CAP_SYS_ADMIN and a fresh observation, then
queues a fresh READ_I1, data-only WRITE_I1 and exact mode/data readback through
the existing shared PCODE owner. Firmware clamping or a changed mode is a
failure, never silently accepted. Administrative transactions retain the port
across their read/write/verify commands and give a queued peer first choice
at completion; passive reads also rotate preference. Ambiguous shared-port
loss closes both power actors. Close/reset discards queued/in-flight work
without replay and retains the original ceiling/mode. DG2 explicitly refuses
I1 in the pinned source; it never receives these commands.

DG2 has two fan counters (`fan1_input`/`fan2_input`); BMG additionally exposes
`fan3_input` where present after owned firmware fan-count discovery. RPM extends
observed pulse deltas with source scaling and wrap/gap/refusal checks.
Two read-only BMG PCODE transactions discover fan
count and package/VRAM thermal limits. This admitted dGPU Running scope owns
the port exclusively (the bound card has no display owner); foreign busy
refuses posting, software command+epoch tracks the pending request, and DATA
is consumed only after its owned completion. Completion has status but no
assumed command echo. Still-busy observations after 1 ms time out without
spinning; close discards the software transaction and never consumes an old
reply in a new epoch. Per-service admission/D0/cap denial latches for all
remaining accesses. Cached thermal limits require a successful current sensor
sample; `telemetry_status` reports unavailable/discovery failures. BMG thermal
files are `temp2_emergency`, `temp2_crit`, `temp2_max`, `temp3_emergency`
and `temp3_crit`, created once and empty until proven. Writable fan/thermal
controls remain open.

BMG cached PMT energy uses the actual first BAR0 PUNIT descriptor described by
Xe's synthetic telemetry header; it does not fabricate a PCI DVSEC or accept
arbitrary GUID/address ranges. The retained GT owner receives the actual BAR
length and validates descriptor type/access/BIR/size/base bounds plus the
fixed qualified remapper aperture before access. Each 1 Hz sample rechecks
full identity, preserves non-telemetry selector fields, selects PUNIT index0
and verifies selector readback before/after its two independent aligned32-bit
counter reads and final identity check. Future SoC/remapper clients must share
this owner before admission. `energy1_input`/label expose card energy and
`energy2_input`/label package energy in microJoules using fixed 2^-14-Joule
units. Each counter extends checked32-bit wrap independently. All-ones data,
changed identity/selector, overflow, backward time or a gap over two seconds
